answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. Consider a yarrow as the anchor of the cost.
